title: Visualization of peripheral nerves of the upper limb with MSOT
summary:
Neuropathy is an umbrella term for diseases of the peripheral nerves (“peripheral” means “at the edge”). This includes all nerves in the body - with the exception of the nerve cells in the brain and spinal cord. These peripheral nerves originate in the spinal cord and travel from there throughout the entire body: to the muscles, skin, internal organs and glands. The nerves are responsible for transmitting stimuli. 
If the peripheral nerves become damaged, the transmission of stimuli is limited or no longer functions at all. Neuropathy usually manifests itself in sensory disturbances such as tingling in the legs, burning sensations and numbness in the feet, as well as nerve pain. 
Up to 30% of the population suffer from neuropathy. In people with diabetes, up to 90% are affected. 
Neuropathy is difficult to detect and therefore often goes unrecognized. This is why there is an urgent need for a method that can visualize peripheral nerves and their damage at an early stage. Such an imaging method would also be beneficial in locating nerves for surgery or local anesthesia. 
MSOT (Multispectral Optoacoustic Tomography) is a new and promising non-invasive imaging technique. MSOT uses ultrasound and near-infrared laser light to visualize tissue, offering advantages over ultrasound alone. 
In this study of 100 people, we want to investigate how well MSOT can detect peripheral nerves and various features of neuropathy. Our research aims to improve the early detection of neuropathy.

interventions.name:
100 participants, all undergoing the following activities:
- survey questionnaire to gather information on demographics, nerve-related
history, and peripheral neuropathy risk factor data such as history of diabetes diagnosis and alcohol consumption history, smoking history (self-reported)
- pulse

n/a

pregnancy;
documented or suspicious light allergy, light intolerance, contact dermatitis, or particularly sensitive skin
